newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Chronology of major political events in Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of major political events in Indonesia.

text.p: Following is a chronology of major political events in Indonesia since it proclaimed independence.

AUG 17, 1945 - Nationalist leaders Sukarno and Hatta, who became president and vice-president of the new republic, make declaration of independence in Jakarta but fighting continues with Dutch colonial forces.
MAY 7, 1949 - Hostilities end between republic and Dutch forces.
DEC 27, 1949 - Sovereignty formally transferred to new republic and 15 states previously established by the Dutch.
MAY 19, 1950 - Agreement between the republic and federal states to restore Unitary Republic of Indonesia with new constitution.
SEPT, 1955 - First general elections held. Sukarno's Indonesian Nationalist Party, two Moslem parties and the Communist Party receive the most votes.
JULY 5, 1959 - President Sukarno declares dissolution of constituent assembly and a return to the 1945 constitution.
MARCH 1960 - Sukarno dissolves parliament.
JUNE, 1960 - Sukarno appoints new "mutual cooperation" parliament.

SEPT 30, 1965 - Six senior army generals killed in what is later described as an abortive communist coup. Major-General Suharto, then commanding the strategic reserve, takes command of the military and crushes coup attempt.
MARCH 11, 1966 - Executive power transferred from President Sukarno to General Suharto.
MARCH 12, 1996 - Suharto bans the Communist Party of Indonesia. This leads to army-backed purges of suspected communists and at least 500,000 people are killed.
MARCH 21, 1967 - Suharto confirmed as president by appointed People's Consultative Assembly (MPR).
JUNE 21, 1970 - Sukarno dies after more than two years of house arrest.
JULY, 1971 - General elections held for parliament, which is then incorporated into larger MPR. Suharto's Golkar party wins more than 62 percent of the vote.

JAN, 1973 - Under government pressure, the United Development Party (PPP) is created from Moslem parties and the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) out of Christian and Nationalist parties. These two minority parties and Golkar are the only groups permitted to contest future elections.

MARCH, 1973 - Suharto appointed unopposed for second five-year presidential term by MPR. He is re-appointed in 1978, 1983, 1988 and 1993 by the MPR after Golkar's easy wins in general elections in 1977, 1982, 1987 and 1992.
JUNE 20, 1996 - Megawati Sukarnoputri, the daughter of Sukarno, is ousted from the leadership of the PDI by a government-backed faction.
JULY 27, 1996 - Riots break out in Jakarta after Megawati loyalists are evicted from PDI headquarters by the rival faction and police.
MARCH, 1997 - Government approves list of candidates for 1997 general elections. Megawati and her supporters are not included.
APRIL 27 - Four-week allotted campaign period for May 29 general elections begins.
MAY 7 - First signs appear that Megawati's supporters are attending PPP rallies. Sporadic violence breaks out in campaign, mostly between PPP and Golkar supporters in Central Java.
MAY 14 - First campaign violence reported in Jakarta. Violence intensifies over subsequent days.
MAY 22 - Megawati says she will not vote in poll but stops short of calling for boycott by her supporters.

MAY 23 - Violence flares in South Kalimantan and across Java as campaign ends. The military says 65 bodies are found in a burned-out shopping complex in the South Kalimantan capital Banjarmasin while four others are killed in Java.
